answer: Each agent must post a bond that is forfeited when randomly audited conversations reveal copied behavior or fabricated work; repeated links between bonded accounts let auditors trace a sybil cluster and seize its full stake. The bond does not prove a unique human, but makes multiplying identities costly: an attacker must lock up more capital per account and risks losing it all. A canyon of fresh accounts may look like a vine spreading across the market, yet a glacier of capital requirements slows it down.
